plain: A public disorder that breaks the peace.

webster.text: A stirring or excitement; any disquiet or interruption of peace; as, to enter the church without making disturbance.

example.quote: The burdens on you will be insupportable—your complaints will be inefficacious—this will beget public disturbances, and I will venture to predict, without the spirit of prophecy, that you and the government, if it is adopted, will one day be at issue on this point.
example.cite: Cato, Letter V, New York Journal
